# PlayGonu

> PlayGonu is a collection of traditional Korean Gonu (고누) strategy board games, plus Gomoku. Every game is playable solo against a built-in AI (four difficulty levels) or online against another real person in real time — no install, no account, no download. Available in English, Korean, Spanish, Japanese and Simplified Chinese.

## Games

- [Cham-gonu](https://playgonu.com/): The main game and PlayGonu's homepage. A 24-point board of three nested squares, 12 pieces per player — place pieces to form three-in-a-row "mills" and capture, then slide once the board fills. Same family as the Western game Nine Men's Morris (its closest relative is Twelve Men's Morris / Morabaraba). Two rulesets are selectable on the game screen: Korean (the default; captured points are locked during placement, 20-move no-capture rule) and Western (Twelve Men's Morris rules: no locked points, flying at exactly 3 pieces).
- [Jul-gonu](https://playgonu.com/jul): The simplest Gonu variant — a 4x4-point line board, 4 pieces per player, sandwich (custodian) capture. A two-minute starter game.
- [Daseotjul-gonu](https://playgonu.com/daseotjul): Jul-gonu's exact rules on a bigger 5x5-point board with 5 pieces per side.
- [Palpal-gonu](https://playgonu.com/palpal): Jul-gonu's exact rules on the widest board in the family — 8x8 points, 8 pieces per side.
- [Bakwi-gonu](https://playgonu.com/bakwi): "Wheel gonu" — 4 pieces per side on a 4x4-point board; a piece standing on one of the board's four corner "wheels" can slide any distance in a straight line and capture the first enemy piece in its path.
- [Gomoku (Omok)](https://playgonu.com/gomoku): The classic five-in-a-row game, not part of the Gonu family — Freestyle or Standard (Renju) rules, 15x15 board.

## Other pages

- [How to Play](https://playgonu.com/howto): Full written rules for every game on the site, in one place.
- [Cham-gonu strategy: the running mill](https://playgonu.com/cham-strategy): How Cham-gonu is usually won — a real game walked through with screenshots, the board's strongest points, and how to build or stop a running mill (a piece shuttling between two mills to capture every turn). Also in Korean, Spanish, Japanese and Chinese.
- [Online Battle](https://playgonu.com/online): Real-time multiplayer for Cham-gonu and Gomoku — create a private room and share the link, or join an open public room. No account needed, just a name.
- [Blog](https://playgonu.com/blog/): Articles on Gonu's history and how it compares to Nine Men's Morris, Gomoku, and Renju.
  - [What Is Gonu? Korea's Ancient Board Game Family, Explained](https://playgonu.com/blog/what-is-gonu)
  - [Cham-gonu: Korea's Version of Nine Men's Morris](https://playgonu.com/blog/cham-gonu-nine-mens-morris)
  - [Gomoku vs. Renju vs. Omok: What's the Difference?](https://playgonu.com/blog/gomoku-vs-renju-vs-omok)
  - [PlayGonu Is Live: Korea's Traditional Board Games, Free and Online](https://playgonu.com/blog/playgonu-launch)
- [Sources and references](https://playgonu.com/sources): The published sources behind the game histories and rules — Korean government and academic references, Wikipedia, and Stewart Culin's 1895 Korean Games — listed per game. Also in Korean, Spanish, Japanese and Chinese.
- [Embed PlayGonu on your site](https://playgonu.com/embed/): Free copy-and-paste iframe code to add Cham-gonu or Gomoku (AI opponent) to a blog or website.
- [오목 전략 가이드 (Korean)](https://playgonu.com/ko/gomoku-strategy): Gomoku/Omok strategy in Korean — open threes, the 4-3 winning shape, Renju forbidden moves (3x3, 4x4, overline), openings, and practice against the AI.
- [퍼가기 코드 (Korean embed guide)](https://playgonu.com/ko/embed/): Free copy-and-paste iframe code in Korean to add Gomoku (오목) or Cham-gonu (참고누) to a blog or website.
- [Privacy Policy](https://playgonu.com/privacy)
- [Korean version (한국어)](https://playgonu.com/ko/): The game pages, how-to and online battle in Korean, at the /ko/ path.
- [Spanish version (Español)](https://playgonu.com/es/): The same pages in Spanish, at /es/.
- [Japanese version (日本語)](https://playgonu.com/ja/): The same pages in Japanese, at /ja/ (Gomoku appears as 五目並べ).
- [Simplified Chinese version (简体中文)](https://playgonu.com/zh/): The same pages in Simplified Chinese, at /zh/ (Gomoku appears as 五子棋).

## About each game page

Every game page has a written article under the board — an at-a-glance fact table, the game's origin, step-by-step rules, tips, a short FAQ, and links to the other games — in all five languages. The sources are listed on the Sources page. Longer sections are folded (HTML <details>) but the full text is in the page source. The same pages carry JSON-LD (Game, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage).
